sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Saginaw, Michigan?
sections.html:
Saginaw sells at some of the lowest home values in the state, so the route you pick matters more than the asking price. The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $60,000 for 2020 to 2024. Price expectations here run well below the state's larger metro areas.

Three paths are open to most owners, and each one trades time, cost and certainty differently:

  • List with an agent. You get the widest buyer pool, but you wait through showings, inspections and a buyer's lender.
  • Sell on your own. You skip the commission and take on the pricing, paperwork and negotiation yourself.
  • Take a cash offer. Cash buyers purchase as-is, which suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant, a vacancy or an estate behind it. Compare more than one offer and read the closing terms.

Whichever path you choose, a short list of city and county steps applies to every Saginaw sale. They are covered below.

sections.h2: What is Saginaw like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Saginaw is the seat of Saginaw County, set on the Saginaw River about 15 miles inland from Saginaw Bay. It covers roughly 17 square miles of land, and Wikipedia notes the city sits in the middle of the largest watershed in Michigan.

The city began as a trading post and fort after the 1819 Treaty of Saginaw, grew on lumber in the 1800s, and became a manufacturing center as General Motors plants multiplied through the twentieth century. East Saginaw and Saginaw City merged in 1889 to form the city you see on the map today.

Factory closures followed. The 2010 census counted 51,508 residents and the 2020 census counted 44,202, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 42,863. Population loss and a long run of vacant houses are part of the backdrop for pricing, so expect buyers to ask hard questions about condition.

Vacant and neglected houses have been a long-running concern. A 2013 federal blight program set aside $11.2 million for Saginaw, and the city then began buying unwanted structures for demolition. If your house is vacant, deal with grass, boarding and utilities early, because an untended property loses value faster than one that looks lived in.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods, schools and roads do Saginaw buyers care about?
sections.html:
Buyers sort Saginaw by neighborhood and by commute. The city names Downtown, Old Town, Southwest Village, Heritage Square, Cathedral District, Brockway-Carmen Park, Sheridan Park, Northmoor and The Woods among its neighborhoods, along with the South East Side, Northeast Side and Northwest areas. Naming the neighborhood in a listing or an offer request tells a buyer what to expect on block condition.

Public schools come from Saginaw Public Schools, which Wikipedia lists with Saginaw United High School and the Saginaw Arts and Sciences Academy as the two public high schools. Michigan Lutheran Seminary is the private high school. Delta College and Saginaw Valley State University are in nearby University Center, and a Delta College downtown site opened in fall 2019.

  • I-75 runs along the east side of the city through Buena Vista Charter Township.
  • I-675 loops through downtown and rejoins I-75.
  • M-13 runs from I-69 through downtown, and M-46 crosses the state east to west through the city.
  • M-47 serves the western suburbs and MBS International Airport.
  • STARS provides local bus service, and Indian Trails serves intercity travelers.

Shopping for the metro area clusters along Bay Road and Tittabawassee Road in Saginaw Township, just north of the city line.

sections.h2: How do winters affect an older Saginaw house?
sections.html:
Saginaw has a humid continental climate, and NOAA normals quoted by Wikipedia show about 49 inches of snow and 32 inches of precipitation in a typical year. The mean low in January is 16.4 degrees Fahrenheit, with a record low of minus 23.

Those numbers put stress on roofs, gutters, foundations and heating systems. Buyers and inspectors in cold-climate Michigan cities look first at the roof, the furnace or boiler, basement moisture and the plumbing in unheated areas. If you know of a past leak, frozen pipe or ice dam, say so up front. Disclosure protects you after closing, and a seller who explains a repair is easier to trust than one whose buyer finds it later.

For a vacant house, keep the heat on at a low setting or have the water shut off and the lines drained before the cold season. A burst pipe in an empty house can turn a sellable property into a gutted one in a single week.

sections.h2: What are the Saginaw rules for rentals and vacant houses?
sections.html:
Saginaw requires non-owner-occupied houses and unoccupied houses to be registered with the City Clerk. The City Council amended these rules in Ordinance O-275, which took effect November 27, 2025. It removed the old requirement that every unpaid tax or rubbish bill be cleared before a property could register, and the city now uses other ways to collect those amounts.

  • A rental owner must register with the Clerk and provide a current certificate of compliance where the code requires one.
  • Rental registrations expire each year on the fourth Friday of February, and a late renewal adds a 100 percent charge to the base fee.
  • A buyer who takes title to a rental or vacant property must register within 60 days of the transfer.
  • An owner who lives in a single-dwelling house, or whose immediate family does, is not required to register that dwelling.
  • An owner who is actively advertising a registered rental for sale or rent does not also have to register it as unoccupied, with a copy of the advertisement as proof.

The unoccupied registry has a 12-month window after purchase for owners who are rehabilitating the house under permit. The Clerk's office, reachable at (989) 759-1480 extension 6, answers registration questions.

sections.h2: How do recording and transfer work for a Saginaw sale?
sections.html:
Deeds for Saginaw property are recorded with the Saginaw County Register of Deeds. The office lists a recording fee of $30 per document under MCL 600.2567, with an extra $3 for each added instrument on a document that assigns or discharges more than one. Copies cost $1 per page, and a certified copy adds $5.

For tax certification, the county's fee page tells you to contact the Saginaw County Treasurer. Ask the Register of Deeds and the Treasurer for the state and county transfer tax rates and for who pays them before closing, so the figure is on your settlement statement in advance.

After the sale, Michigan Treasury guidance says the buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, with the local assessor within 45 days of a transfer, citing MCL 211.27a(10). Property tax bills and any city utility balances should be settled through the closing agent so that nothing follows you to the next owner.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Saginaw that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Saginaw houses with deferred repairs sell to investors and cash buyers who purchase as-is. Expect the price to reflect the repair cost, and gather permits, receipts and a list of known problems before you ask for offers.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my Saginaw rental before selling it?
faqs.a: A rental you own has to be registered with the City Clerk while it is occupied by someone other than you, with annual renewal due the fourth Friday of February. The buyer then registers within 60 days of taking title. Call the Clerk at (989) 759-1480 extension 6 for your situation.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Saginaw County?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds lists $30 per document for recording. Transfer tax and tax certification are separate, so ask the Register of Deeds and the County Treasurer for the current figures before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who files the Property Transfer Affidavit after a Saginaw sale?
faqs.a: The buyer files it. Michigan Treasury guidance sets a 45-day window from the transfer for Form 2766, filed with the local assessor. Mention it to your title company so the buyer is reminded.

faqs.q: Is Saginaw a hard place to sell a house?
faqs.a: Prices are low and the population has fallen from 51,508 in 2010 to an estimated 42,863 in July 2025, so patience and a realistic price matter. Clean, documented houses in steady neighborhoods still find buyers, and a cash sale avoids the delay of a buyer's loan approval.
